newsitem.title: UK: UK Budget - Who said what.
newsitem.headline: UK Budget - Who said what.

text.p: Following are a selection of comments on Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's budget speech to Britain's parliament on Tuesday:
-- "There was no white rabbit coming out of the hat, instead another gerbil. This was a re-run of last year." -- GERARD LYONS, chief economist at DKB International.

-- "People will judge the budget as one of five in which they are paying 2,000 pounds more in tax cumulatively after all the promises made by the Conservatives." -- GORDON BROWN, main opposition Labour Party's shadow Chancellor.

-- "The PSBR forecasts were very realistic because of the upward growth revisions -- maybe balancing the budget by the year 2000 is a little bit optimistic." -- IAN AMSTAD, senior economist at Bankers Trust.
-- "For individuals it is a case of gain this year and pain next year." -- DOUGLAS FAIRBAIRN, national tax partner at accountants Ernst & Young.

-- "The proposals this afternoon will not put a single nurse into a hospital or a single extra teacher into a school. The Tories are at it again." -- ALISTAIR DARLING, Labour Party's shadow Chief Treasury Secretary.
--"Sterling just loves this budget because there's tax cutting into growing consumer expenditure and that will mean higher interest rates." -- PETER VON MAYDELL, senior currency economist at UBS.

-- "I think there's a danger he's trying to squeeze a quart out of a pint pot to pay for tax cuts by reducing tax leakage and cutting down on tax abuses." -- ANDREW SENTANCE, economist at London Business School.
-- "It is not an election-winning budget if it tends to give away an awful lot of money we can't afford to give away." -- JOHN REDWOOD, Conservative member of parliament.

-- "Within three months interest rates will go up, or if they don't go up, they ought to go up and the only reason they don't is that the government has an election coming," -- PADDY ASHDOWN, leader of opposition Liberal Democrats party.
-- "We think it's well-judged. The Chancellor has resisted pressure for a big pre-election giveaway. -- RUPERT HODGES, communications director at the British Retail Consortium.
